Om provet som helhet är hennes omdöme tydligt, men inte villkorslöst:

– Jag skulle välja att göra provet igen. Att ha en samlad vy över felanmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle ge förberedelserna en vecka till.

Någon rekommendation av Svale till alla bostadsbolag ger hon inte.

| 24 | "Provet har ännu inte utvidgats. Underhållsteamet fattar beslut om det när det har sett hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer." | "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." | None. | Supported |
| 25 | "Den som planerar ett eget prov kan läsa [checklistan för implementering](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist) innan planeringen börjar." | "The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist ...; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial." | The link is accurately described as a checklist to read. The rest is advice. | Supported |

Terms carried across languages:
- "felanmälan/felanmälningar" for "repair report(s)": both name reports of a repair need. I found no case in this context that falls under one term and not the other.
- "arbetsledare" for "supervisor": same.
- "anställda" for "staff": same.
- "akuta ärenden" for "emergencies": same.
- "hus" for "buildings": same.

## B. Pronoun accounting

- **"hon"** (lead paragraph and the paragraph after quote 3) refers to Maya Lind. It is third person singular and asserts female natural gender. The source supports this: "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment."
- **"det"** refers to "underhållsteamet" (rows 10 and 24, "testade det", "när det har sett"). It is third person singular with neuter grammatical gender and makes no natural-gender assertion. This matches the source's "It chose..." and "the team".
- **"det"** refers to "provet" ("hur hon värderar det") and to the expansion ("beslut om det"). Both are grammatical neuter only.
- **"de"** ("vad de inte kan visa") refers to "mätningarna" and **"dem"** (heading, row 9) refers to "kategorierna". Both are third person plural with no gender.
- **"vi/oss/våra"** in quotes 1–3 correspond to the source's "we/us/ours" (first person plural). **"jag"** corresponds to "I" (first person singular). Person and number are kept.
- **"Den som planerar"** is generic and asserts no gender.

## C. Translation of quotations

- **Q1:** "Kategorierna var våra egna" renders the stressed "ours" idiomatically and adds nothing. Splitting the semicolon into two sentences keeps the meaning. "Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem" keeps "helped". No obstruction.
- **Q2:** "komma överens om", "föra in", "avsätta den tiden" and "kommer i gång" are idiomatic. The comparison and the conditional "skulle" are kept. No obstruction.
- **Q3:** "en samlad vy" is a faithful rendering of "one view". "ge förberedelserna en vecka till" matches "leave an extra week for preparation". The conditional, the qualification ("men") and the stance are kept. No obstruction.

No translation findings.

## D. Observations (not defects)

- **"orsaken lämnas öppen" (heading, row 14).** In the article's own voice this is accurate: the draft assigns no cause. The source does not say whether the note names workload as the cause. The heading's passive does not assert that it does not, so this is defensible. If the editor wants the heading to state exactly what is known, "– anteckningen tillskriver inte programvaran skillnaden" would do it.
- **Supplier-published status.** The source says the case is "supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism". The draft makes no claim of independence, so nothing in the draft contradicts this. Whether to disclose the status is an editorial question outside this comparison.

## E. Findings (source support)

**F1. Title turns Lind's assessment into the publisher's factual claim.**
- Draft: "Samlad vy över felanmälningar hjälper Elm Quays team".
- Source: only Lind: "Having one view of the reports helps us". There is no measurement of benefit ("There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements"), and the note "explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software".
- Case: Lind finds the single view helpful, but other team members do not, or no benefit is measurable. The source statement (Lind says it helps) holds; the title's unattributed claim fails. Nothing in the material excludes this.
- The article is published by the supplier, so the unattributed title reads as Svale asserting an effect.
- Repair: attribute it, e.g. "Arbetsledaren på Elm Quay: En samlad vy över felanmälningarna hjälper oss".

**F2. Heading makes Svale the one who entered the categories.**
- Draft: "Teamet bestämde kategorierna och Svale lade in dem".
- Source: "Svale helped us put them into the log"; "Svale configured the log".
- Case: Elm Quay's staff entered the categories themselves, with Svale guiding them. The source holds and the heading fails. "Svale configured the log" does not exclude this case.
- The error also moves an action from the customer to the supplier, although the brief asks for the customer to stay the acting party.
- Repair: "Teamet bestämde kategorierna och Svale hjälpte till att lägga in dem".

**F3 (minor). "emails" narrowed to emailed fault reports.**
- Draft: "felanmälningar som kom in per telefon och per mejl".
- Source: "telephone reports and emails were stored separately."
- Case: the separately stored emails included internal staff or contractor emails that were not fault reports. The source holds and the draft fails. No supplied statement excludes this.
- Repair: "Tidigare sparades telefonanmälningar och mejl var för sig."

**F4. Heading drops the scope of the median.**
- Draft heading: "Mediantiden blev kortare".
- Source: "Median time from report to assignment ..."
- The unqualified heading can be read as median repair (completion) time. The source says there are none: "There are no ... completion-time measurements". The brief also warns: "Do not turn assignment time into completion time." The base contract requires scope to be kept in headings.
- Case: completion time did not shorten, or was never measured, while assignment time did. The heading, read as completion time, fails.
- Repair: "Mediantiden till fördelning blev kortare – orsaken lämnas öppen".

## Completion status

Complete. Four source-support findings are unresolved in the draft: F1, F2, F3 (minor) and F4. There are no translation findings. Section D lists two editorial observations that are not defects.

"Swedish is a V2 language: the finite verb is the second constituent of a main clause, so fronting anything at all pushes the subject behind the verb. Write *I morgon åker vi till Malmö*, never *I morgon vi åker till Malmö*. This is the single most common structural tell of a text drafted in English and rendered into Swedish.

Compounds are written as one word. *Kvalitetssäkring*, *kundtjänstmedarbetare*, *miljökonsekvensbeskrivning*. Splitting them is not a stylistic choice in Swedish and often changes the meaning outright — *en rökfri miljö* and *en rök fri miljö* are different claims. Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

The s-passive is the ordinary Swedish passive and is shorter than its periphrastic alternative: *rapporten skickas på fredag*, not *rapporten blir skickad på fredag*. Both exist; the s-form is the unmarked one, and the *bli*-form carries a change-of-state reading that is often not intended.

*Du* is the default address in Swedish prose, including business and journalism. *Ni* to a single reader is either archaic or a deliberate distancing, and reads as a translation from a language that has a formal pronoun.

*Man* is a fallback rather than the ordinary generic pronoun. It is justified where the agent genuinely is anybody at all or is genuinely unknown, and where naming one would claim more than the material carries. Where the sentence has a real subject to hand — the reader, the writer, the organisation, the profession, the study — that subject is what the sentence takes. Swedish tolerates a shorter sentence than English does and punishes subordination harder. Prefer a main clause with a fronted adverbial to a long relative construction, and prefer a verb to a nominalisation: *när kommunen beslutade* over *vid kommunens beslutsfattande*.

Reach for the established Swedish term where one exists and the field actually uses it — *återkoppling*, *underlag*, *avstämning* — but do not purge the loanwords a professional reader expects. # Source-fidelity report 2: draft.md against source.md

Draft language: Swedish (sv). Source language: English. Quotations of Maya Lind are translated; the material permits translation "preserving stance and qualification". The byline comes from the invocation and is outside this check.

## A. Claim accounting

Each row gives the draft passage, the source passage it rests on (verbatim, English), and what differs.

### Title and lede

1. **Draft (title):** "Samlad vy hjälper teamet, bedömer Elm Quays arbetsledare"
   **Source:** "Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation." / "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment." / "maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"
   **Difference:** *bedömer* keeps this as Lind's assessment, which is supported. The beneficiary is narrowed: the source's "us" becomes *teamet*. Nothing in the material says who "us" is. Lind speaks as maintenance supervisor, and "us" could just as well mean Elm Quay Housing as an organisation, or a group wider than the trial team (for example, the staff who take telephone reports). Case: the single view helps Elm Quay as an organisation, for instance through management oversight, and that is what Lind means, with no specific claim about the maintenance team. The source holds and the title fails. No supplied statement excludes this case. -> **Finding S1.** The "but" qualification in the source applies to "choose to do the trial again", not to "helps us", so the title does not lose a qualification. *Elm Quays arbetsledare* leaves out "maintenance", but that makes no false claim.

2. **Draft (lede):** "Under åtta veckor provade Elm Quay Housing en gemensam logg för felanmälningar i två hus."
   **Source:** "its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings" / "The trial lasted eight weeks."
   **Difference:** The subject is the company rather than its maintenance team. The team is part of the company and the brief wants Elm Quay as the acting party, so no case separates the two. "Repair log" becomes *logg för felanmälningar*. The source's entries are "repair reports" that run "from report to assignment", which are fault reports in the *felanmälan* sense. No difference.

3. **Draft (lede):** "Arbetsledaren Maya Lind skulle göra om provet, men med en extra vecka för förberedelser."
   **Source:** "I would choose to do the trial again. … but I would leave an extra week for preparation."
   **Difference:** The conditional mood and the qualification are both kept. No difference.

4. **Draft (lede):** "Här är hur underhållsteamet lade upp arbetet, vad mätningarna visar och vad de inte kan visa."
   **Source:** Rests on the process and measurement passages below, and on "the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements."
   **Difference:** This is the author's framing and rests on supported material. No difference.

### Body

5. **Draft:** "Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter."
   **Source:** "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats."
   **Difference:** None.

6. **Draft:** "Tidigare sparades telefonanmälningar och mejl var för sig."
   **Source:** "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately."
   **Difference:** None.

7. **Draft:** "I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att prova en gemensam felanmälningslogg i två av husen."
   **Source:** "In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings."
   **Difference:** The date attaches to the decision, as in the source. The draft does not say the trial started in September. No difference.

8. **Draft:** "Maya Lind, arbetsledare för underhållet, beskriver vad provet krävde och hur hon värderar det."
   **Source:** "Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind" / "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment."
   **Difference:** None. For the pronoun, see section B.

9. **Draft (heading):** "Teamet utformade kategorierna, Svale hjälpte till att lägga in dem"
   **Source:** "The maintenance team designed its categories" / "The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log." / "Svale configured the log"
   **Difference:** None.

10. **Draft:** "Innan underhållsteamet valde Svale Systems testade det om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation."
    **Source:** "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair."
    **Difference:** The order of events is kept. The draft claims no comparison with another supplier, which is consistent with "No comparison with another supplier is available." No difference.

11. **Draft:** "De boende kunde fortsätta att felanmäla per telefon."
    **Source:** "kept telephone reporting open for residents"
    **Difference:** The team's decision is recast as what residents could do. The factual content is the same and no case separates the two.

12. **Draft:** "Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex anställda vid två tillfällen. Provet pågick i åtta veckor."
    **Source:** "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks."
    **Difference:** None. The supplier is narrated in the third person.

13. **Draft (heading):** "Mediantiden till fördelning blev kortare – orsaken lämnas öppen"
    **Source:** "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
    **Difference:** *Blev kortare* describes the change from one period to the next. It is a sequence, not a cause, and the heading explicitly leaves the cause open. The measure stays assignment time and is not turned into completion time. *Orsaken lämnas öppen* is the article's own position on the state of knowledge, and it rests on the material: the note does not attribute the difference to the software, and the workloads differed. No difference.

14. **Draft:** "Enligt Elm Quays interna anteckning om provet, daterad den 4 december 2025, fördes 31 felanmälningar in i loggen. Akuta ärenden och arbeten som beställdes före provet ingår inte."
    **Source:** "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial."
    **Difference:** In the source, the note does the excluding ("It excludes"). The draft drops that subject. Because *ingår inte* follows directly on *fördes … in i loggen*, it can be read as saying these items were not included in the log. Case: emergencies were entered in the log and the note left them out of its figures. The source holds and the log reading of the draft fails. No supplied statement says whether emergencies were logged. -> **Finding S2.**

15. **Draft:** "Mediantiden från felanmälan till att ärendet fördelades var två arbetsdagar under provet, mot tre under de åtta veckorna innan. Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna, och anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden."
    **Source:** Same passage as row 13.
    **Difference:** The figures, the unit (working days), the comparison period, the workload caveat and the note's explicit non-attribution are all kept. No difference.

16. **Draft:** "Det finns inga mätningar av kostnader, de boendes nöjdhet eller tiden tills reparationerna var klara."
    **Source:** "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements."
    **Difference:** None.

17. **Draft (heading):** "Arbetsledaren skulle göra om provet med mer förberedelse"
    **Source:** "I would choose to do the trial again. … but I would leave an extra week for preparation." / "I would set that time aside before the next building starts."
    **Difference:** The conditional and the reservation are kept. No difference.

18. **Draft:** "– … skriver Lind." and "– … skriver hon om provet som helhet."
    **Source:** "All interviews occurred by email" / "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment."
    **Difference:** *Skriver* matches an email interview. *Om provet som helhet* describes the third quotation as her overall view of the trial, which is consistent with "her actual, qualified assessment" and with the quotation's content ("do the trial again"). No case separates them.

19. **Draft:** "Någon rekommendation av Svale till alla bostadsbolag ger hon inte."
    **Source:** "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company."
    **Difference:** The scope is kept: she did not recommend Svale to every company, which is not the same as recommending it to none. The source's past tense becomes the present tense, which is ordinary reporting use. No difference.

20. **Draft (heading):** "Teamet ska pröva kategorierna på större reparationer först"
    **Source:** "the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs"
    **Difference:** *Pröva … på* ("try on") renders "checking how … work for", and *först* ("first") renders "decide after". No difference.

21. **Draft:** "Provet har ännu inte utvidgats. Underhållsteamet fattar beslut om det när det har sett hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer."
    **Source:** "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
    **Difference:** None.

22. **Draft:** "Den som planerar ett eget prov kan läsa [checklistan för implementering](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist) innan planeringen börjar."
    **Source:** "The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial."
    **Difference:** The link text and the verb *läsa* ("read") describe the destination accurately. No difference.

### Quotations (source support)

23. **Q1, draft:** "Vi ville att kvällspasset skulle se vad morgonpasset redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra egna. Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen"
    **Source:** "We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log."
    **Difference:** None.

24. **Q2, draft:** "Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att föra in de första felanmälningarna. Den tiden skulle jag avsätta innan nästa hus kommer i gång"
    **Source:** "We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts."
    **Difference:** None.

25. **Q3, draft:** "Jag skulle välja att göra provet igen. Att ha en samlad vy över felanmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle ge förberedelserna en vecka till"
    **Source:** "I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation."
    **Difference:** None. The stance, the conditional and the "but" reservation are all kept.

### Material not used (omissions; no false claim results)

- "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information." This is carried by Q1.
- "No comparison with another supplier is available." The draft claims no comparison.
- "The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism." See editorial question E1.

## B. Pronouns: person, number and natural gender

- *hon* ("she"; rows 8, 18, 19) refers to Maya Lind: third person singular, feminine natural gender. It is supported by the source's own "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment." No finding.
- *det* ("it") in "testade det", "beslut om det" and "när det har sett": in the first and third it refers to *underhållsteamet* ("the maintenance team"), and in the second to the expansion of the trial. It is third person singular with neuter grammatical gender only and asserts no natural gender. Number is consistent with "the team … it chose" in the source. No finding.
- *de* ("they") in the lede ("vad de inte kan visa") refers to *mätningarna* ("the measurements"): third person plural, non-personal. No finding.
- *vi/oss/jag* ("we/us/I") inside the quotations keep the source's person and number: "We", "us", "ours" and "I". The referent of "us" in the title is treated under S1.

## C. Findings: source support

**S1. The title narrows Lind's "us" to "the team".**
- Draft: "Samlad vy hjälper teamet, bedömer Elm Quays arbetsledare"
